vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Renovate applies vulnerabilityAlerts on top of packageRules with groupName: null, which would split a coupled pair into two PRs where either half alone is uninstallable. Naming the group keeps security bumps inside it.

packageRules.description: onnxruntime-gpu and tensorrt-cu13 are coupled: onnxruntime-gpu links libnvinfer.so.10, so they must move together or the TensorRT provider silently fails to load. Automerge here is only safe because the docker-build-check job resolves libonnxruntime_providers_tensorrt.so against the shipped tensorrt_libs with ldd, so a soname drift fails the PR instead of merging quietly. Do not automerge this group if that check is ever removed or weakened to an availability listing, which reports a provider that cannot actually load.

A tensorrt-cu13 major bump changes the libnvinfer soname. onnxruntime-gpu then cannot load the provider and ONNX Runtime falls back to CUDA silently - no error, roughly 5x less throughput. Never automerge that; a human must move onnxruntime-gpu in lockstep.

The runtime stage relocates a --copies venv built on the NGC base (Ubuntu 24.04 / python3.12). A venv loads its stdlib from base_prefix, so the runtime must ship the same python minor. Bumping ubuntu to 26.04 (resolute) dropped the python3.12 package and broke the Docker Build Check. Majors need the python3.x pin moved in lockstep, so hold them for a human.

The NGC TensorRT image is what the aarch64 ONNX Runtime wheel is compiled against, so its TensorRT major is coupled to the tensorrt-cu13 pin in requirements.txt. Bumping it alone is a soname break: 26.02 ships TensorRT 10 and 26.08 ships 11, and an automerged bump to 26.08 produced a wheel needing libnvinfer.so.11 in an image shipping libnvinfer.so.10 - caught by the ldd check in docker/Dockerfile, but only after a 232-minute wheel build. A human must move this and tensorrt-cu13 together. docker/Dockerfile.ortwheel now fails in seconds if they disagree, but that is a backstop, not a reason to automerge.
